hard_cases: Clean baseline: primary + 2 secondary diagnoses and 2 procedures.
Two pages: discharge instructions and the physician sign-off are on page 2.

fields.discharge_instructions: Complete the full course of oral antibiotics. Check blood glucose twice daily and keep a written record. Take blood pressure medication as before. Return to the emergency department immediately if fever above 38.5 C, shortness of breath or chest pain recurs.

extra.address: 1 Arun Amarin Road, Bangkok Noi, Bangkok 10700, Thailand
course: The patient presented with a 4-day history of productive cough, fever up to 39.2 C and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. Chest X-ray on admission showed right lower lobe consolidation. Admission blood glucose was 286 mg/dL.

Intravenous ceftriaxone and oral azithromycin were started. Because of slow clinical response by day 3, bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage was performed; cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae sensitive to the current regimen.

Fever settled on day 4 and oxygen was weaned to room air on day 5. Insulin was used during admission and the patient was switched back to oral agents before discharge. Blood pressure remained controlled on her usual medication.
discharge_meds: Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875/125 mg, 1 tablet twice daily for 5 more days
Metformin 1000 mg, 1 tablet twice daily with meals
extra.follow_up: Respiratory clinic in 2 weeks with repeat chest X-ray. Diabetes clinic in 4 weeks with HbA1c.
